name: core-loop-visual
description: Visual verification of the full core gameplay loop: survey → drill plan → charge → sequence → blast → fragments → contract delivery. Multi-angle screenshots at each phase to confirm smooth transitions and visual feedback.

steps.description: campaign start replaces any prior site entirely with dusty_hollow's own fixed 96x96 grid. #553: cash bumped from $50,000 to $200,000 to cover the driller/drill_rig ($36,000) this file now needs on top of its existing surveyor hire, plus payroll/upkeep during the drilling wait.

Corrected from bare positional args (`employee assign_skill 1 geology 3`), which the command silently rejects (`skill`/`level` are named params, per assignSkillCommand's own usage string) -- Finding #15's class, the same syntax bug caught earlier in survey-confidence-overlay.json. Left unmarked: hiring already grants the Rookie starting qualification (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION in Employee.ts); this only raises the level for the scenario's needs -- the player-facing path is `employee train`.
Not long enough for the surveyor to walk to (20,20) and complete the survey (arrival-gated, #437) -- this file's own core-loop demonstration doesn't wait on it, moving straight to drilling instead.

expect.note: confirmed via direct trace: cash stays flat here -- with only 1 employee and no buildings/vehicles yet, payroll doesn't cycle within just 5 ticks

steps.description: Resolved through the event dialog's own buttons. Decides whether an event is pending from authoritative game state, not from whether the modal has rendered -- a DOM-only probe silently missed events on a no-GPU runner where a frame costs ~6s, leaving them pending so later ticks halted and the run diverged while still passing command mode.

#553: drill_hole is now a queued, vehicle-gated action -- a driller physically drives a drill_rig to each hole -- so this file (which pre-#553 never needed a driller at all) now needs one. campaign start has no staffed:true equivalent, so this is a manual hire + purchase, same pattern as survey-then-blast.json. Employee #2 -- #1 is the surveyor hired above.

Left unmarked: hiring already grants blasting at Rookie (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION), but no role starts with driving.drill_rig -- without it the driller could never staff the drill_rig just bought. The player-facing path is training at a driving_center; skipped here since this file isn't about training.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:2 cols:2 spacing:3 depth:6 start:20,20
steps.description: Corrected from the original rows:3 cols:3 spacing:5 (which command mode ran literally, producing 9 holes): the click drags the (20,20)-(30,30) rectangle at the Drill panel's own default spacing (DEFAULT_SPACING_M=3), computing cols/rows as round(size/spacing)+1 = 4x4 = 16 holes for that same rectangle -- the command and the click were silently testing two different grids, the same class of bug already fixed in nav-cell-types-visual.json. Caught by adding expect.equals.holeCount; fixed by describing what the click actually produces. depth corrected from 8 to 6 (Ground rule #15/Finding #42's class, the whole-suite audit before Phase 3): this step never clicks the grid tool's depth stepper (data-field="depth"), so the real drag always produces the panel's own 6m default regardless of what's declared. This file's own expect blocks only assert hole/charge/sequence counts around the affected blast (depth-insensitive), so this is a metadata-only correction -- verified both modes still pass unchanged. #553: shrunk from 4x4 (16 holes) to 2x2 (4 holes) -- this file demonstrates the core gameplay loop end to end, not blast density, and a single driller cannot land 16 holes without risking a worker_revolt (sandbox-measured elsewhere in this pass). Drag rectangle previously 'corrected' to (20,20)-(26,26), but that arithmetic was wrong: a 6x6 span at spacing 3 is round(6/3)+1 = round(2)+1 = 3, a 3x3=9 grid (reproduced: orderedHoleCount came back 9, not 4). Drill.ts's real formula is cols/rows = Math.max(1, Math.round((x2-x1)/spacing)+1) (blastSteps/Drill.ts:286-287,304-305) -- to land exactly 2 per axis needs round(size/3)=1, i.e. size in [1.5,4.5). Re-corrected to (20,20)-(23,23), a 3x3 span: round(3/3)+1 = 1+1 = 2, a true 2x2=4-hole grid.
#553: drain the ordered plan in bounded 50-tick chunks -- each chunk is followed by `event choose 0` since a `tick` command stops dead the instant a timer event fires mid-block (events.ts).

Third and final chunk — all 4 holes should have landed by now. Two further chunks (150->250 ticks) were dropped here (#554-followup, issue #586 CI): a direct trace showed all 4 holes already landed by tick 155 (end of this chunk) with orderedHoleCount already 0, so the extra 100 ticks the file used to spend past that point were pure padding -- and exactly that padding, on a 2-employee crew with no living quarters ever built in this file, was enough for wellBeing (already pinned at 0 by ~tick135) to accumulate REVOLT_TICKS=120 consecutive ticks at zero and end the level via worker_revolt (WorkerRevolt.ts) before charging ever got a chance to run as real, clickable UI -- the interaction-mode wait_until step below needs the speed-8x control to still be usable, which a worker_revolt's full-viewport LevelEndScreen overlay permanently prevents. Trimming the dead padding keeps the level alive long enough for charge/sequence/blast to run as genuine player interaction instead of falling back to the guard-step pattern.

#554-followup (issue #586 CI): restored to a real click. Trimming the dead tick-50 padding above (see that step's own description) keeps the level alive past this point -- worker_revolt no longer fires before charging, so the full-viewport LevelEndScreen overlay this step used to guard against never appears here, and charge-all is genuinely reachable the same way blast-basic.json's own charge-all click is.

#554-followup (issue #586 CI, two independent agents confirmed a 900000ms single waitUntil still stalls): root cause is the event-freeze asymmetry already fixed elsewhere in this batch (blast-execution-visual.json, level1-lose-ecology.json, level3-playthrough-ecology.json) -- command mode's own waitUntil (command-runner.ts) auto-resolves any pending random event every tick it advances, interaction mode's waitUntil (interaction-executor.ts) never does, by design (its real, isPaused-gated clock halts exactly as it would for a real player). This file's own 2-employee crew, pinned at wellBeing 0 for long stretches (no living quarters anywhere in the file), is exactly the kind of scenario a spontaneous event fires into mid-wait. Chunked into the same tick-N/event-choose-0 pair pattern already used for this file's own drilling waits above (NOT a single step with a resolveEventIfPending tucked into its interaction array -- command-runner.ts only special-cases a step whose interaction array contains a literal `waitUntil` action; every other step, in command mode, just runs its own top-level `command` string once and ignores the rest of the interaction array, so a resolveEventIfPending sitting next to a `command` action inside one step never runs in command mode at all. A pending event left over from a prior chunk's tick then blocks every later tick from advancing, which is exactly what command mode sandbox-testing this fix surfaced: chargedCount stuck at 0 even after ~3000 ticks). #554-followup round 2 (issue #586 CI, real failure): the first pass of this fix used 10 rounds (200 ticks) as a flat safety margin, reasoning by analogy to this file's own ~150-tick drilling wait -- sandbox-measured, that was badly oversized: chargedCount actually reaches 4 by round 3 (tick 205), so 7 of the 10 rounds were dead padding, and with wellBeing pinned at 0 almost the entire time, that padding is exactly the dead-tick-padding-into-revolt pattern this file already hit once this session (this time pushing tickCount, not intentionally, into the same REVOLT_TICKS=120 danger zone the original padding-removal fix was written to avoid) -- real CI's own worker_revolt sometimes fires during those extra idle rounds, covering the panel before the sequence step below ever runs. Trimmed to 4 rounds (80 ticks, sandbox-confirmed complete by round 3 with one round of margin) instead.

Defensive no-op (resolveEventIfPending) -- the chunked wait above already resolves any event that fires during its own tick loop, but interaction mode's real clock can still leave one pending in the gap between the last chunk's tick and this step starting.
Restore normal speed before the remaining player-driven steps, matching blast-basic.json's own convention.
#554-followup (issue #586 CI): restored to a real click, same reason as the charge-all step above -- the level is alive again by this point.

This file never buys any software tier, so the preview prints '[Requires software tier N]' for every section (see safety-projection-visual.json for the unlocked version) -- still a real, clickable control either way. #554-followup (issue #586 CI): restored to a real click -- the level is alive again by this point (see the charge-all step's description above), so run-analysis is genuinely reachable, not covered by a level-end overlay. #554-followup round 2 (issue #586 CI, real failure): 'element has zero size (0x0)' -- run-analysis lives on the Preview tab ([data-step="4"]), which the panel never auto-navigates to on its own (BlastWorkshop.ts's suggestStep only advances through drill/charge/sequence); the panel was still showing the Sequence tab from the auto-sequence step above, so run-analysis's own tab content was display:none. Added the missing tab click, matching the same panel-still-on-a-different-tab class already fixed elsewhere this session (blast-execution-visual.json, level3-playthrough-ecology.json).
#554-followup (issue #586 CI): restored to a real click sequence (execute -> confirm -> report close), same reason as the steps above -- matches blast-basic.json's own execute flow.

#513/#581: the accept click is scoped by contract type, not a fixed id -- `data-contract-type` (ContractsPanel's `makeOfferedCard`) names a contract by what it actually is (#554/#597's `type:`/`material:` ContractSelector convention), immune to the tick-based offer pool's own id drift. #554-followup (issue #586 CI): restored to a real click -- trimming the dead tick-50 padding earlier in this file (see that step's own description) keeps the level alive past the charge/sequence/blast steps, so the contracts panel is genuinely reachable here too, not covered by a level-end overlay.

BLOCKED for a real, load-bearing reason: the ACTIVE card's DELIVER button is genuinely disabled (ContractsPanel disables the amount box, MAX and DELIVER together whenever maxDeliverable = min(contract remaining, stored material) is 0, and a direct trace of this file shows 0.0 kg in storage -- this file never buys a hauling vehicle or hires a driver, so nothing ever reaches storage). The console command is no better: it returns success:false and command mode only fails a step on a thrown exception, so this is a silent no-op in both modes today. `expect.blocked` pins the real control down by contract type, same convention as the accept step above, rather than the toolbar-level overlay guard this step used before the level-end padding fix -- the contracts panel itself is reachable now, only this specific card's DELIVER button is genuinely disabled. Forcing a click here would be asserting something the game correctly forbids.

expect.note: the contract stays active/undelivered -- this file's own "contract delivery" step in its description is a queued attempt, not a completed one; economy-full-loop.json is the file that actually hauls stock and completes a delivery.
